tagline: Fifty-four miles from the Pettus Bridge to the Capitol steps.
intro: The byway leaves Selma over the Edmund Pettus Bridge, which starts high on the town's bluff and comes down across the Alabama River, then follows US 80 east through the low hills of Lowndes County to the Capitol in Montgomery. It is the route of the voting rights march of March 1965, and markers along it show where the marchers camped.

In 1965 the road ran four lanes out of Selma, narrowed to two through Lowndes County and widened again at the Montgomery County line. A court order held the march to 300 people on the two-lane stretch. They crossed it in two days of cold rain, camping in muddy fields.

moments.title: Edmund Pettus Bridge
moments.text: On March 7, 1965, police met the marchers here with horses, clubs and tear gas. On March 21 they crossed it again and kept walking to Montgomery.

moments.title: Lowndes Interpretive Center, White Hall
moments.text: The trail's center stands in the county where, in 1965, Black residents were 81 percent of the population and not one of them was registered to vote.

moments.title: Alabama State Capitol
moments.text: On March 25, 25,000 people marched in from the City of St. Jude to these steps, where King gave the speech remembered as How Long, Not Long.
